question: Can selective Rust rewrites reduce warm Voiceour computation while preserving recognized text on the fixed corpus?
conclusion: Yes for these implementations/inputs/hardware; no evidence the decoder language itself causes the gain because the equivalent C control matches it.

boundary.timed: decoded mono PCM -> mel -> native Metal encoder with current-row shape preparation -> tail -> segment/token rendering -> TokenMapping -> LiteralComposition -> CleanupEngine(empty glossary)

limitations: One M4 Pro, macOS27.0.1; no population or global fastest claim.
Per-row median then paired row bootstrap; correlated speakers/terms and repeated runs are not independent population evidence.
Probability floats differ even when tokens/text/timestamps agree; confidence behavior is not proven identical.
C-control shares the Rust mel; it isolates decoder implementation language only.
Native Metal default is the full-path baseline, not the existing optional CPU tail.
Nine-thread optimized CPU tail vs native defaults; concurrency, algorithms, compilers and language are not one-factor matched.
Only <=34.955s inputs; dynamic shape growth above50s unmeasured.
Energy, packaging, cancellation, interactive contention and cross-SoC qualification required before shipping.

run_meta.notes: elapsed_us: one arm's wall time from raw 16 kHz mono f32 PCM to the final cleaned text, on ONE shared ParakeetContext (the sidecar's own construction: pinned model, weight arena, Metal tail, 6 threads). UNTIMED: the WAV read and Int16-to-f32 conversion (WAVFile.readSamples, done once per row and pass and handed to every arm as the same array), the audio digest and sample-count checks (before the first pass), resetting the native stage counters, poisoning the Rust output buffers with NaN, and everything after the last stage mark (hashes, token reads, the comparisons). TIMED, every arm: the stage chain below, then TokenMapping.transcript, LiteralComposition.apply and CleanupEngine.clean with an empty glossary; a stage mark is one monotonic clock read, taken inside the timer by every arm, so work.stages_us sums to elapsed_us. native and native@aa: ParakeetContext.transcribe (parakeet_full: mel, the encoder with its per-row shape preparation, the Metal tail, segment collection). rust-tail: parakeet_pcm_to_mel, parakeet_encode_stored_mel (this row's graph shape prepared inside the call: no_context reset, audio context, high-water-mark reservation), parakeet_copy_encoder_states into a preallocated host buffer, vt_decode with the --rust-tail-arm engine, ParakeetContext.assembleSegments (token pieces from the native vocabulary via parakeet_token_to_str/_text, the tail's t0/t1, punctuation collapse and word-start rule). rust-mel: vm_compute with the --rust-mel-arm engine into a preallocated buffer, parakeet_set_mel (a copy into the state), parakeet_full over the stored mel (native encoder and Metal tail), collectSegments. rust-mel-tail: vm_compute, parakeet_set_mel, parakeet_encode_stored_mel, state copy-out, vt_decode with the Rust tail, assembleSegments. c-control: rust-mel-tail with the --c-tail-arm tail, the same Rust mel and native encoder. No arm is primed by an untimed decode; pass 0 is a discarded warmup of the whole grid. NOT measured: microphone capture, focus, insertion, cancellation, the sidecar IPC, stage overlap or pipelining across arms. Candidates never read the dump's mel or encoder states; the dump supplies audio_path, audio_sha256 and the reference tokens and text. Validation per row and pass, after the last arm: tokens_equal_ref = canonical token string digest equals the dump ref; text_equal_ref = the raw transcript equals the dump ref text; final_equal_ref = the final text equals CleanupEngine.clean(LiteralComposition.apply(ref text)); *_equal_native = the same comparisons against this row's native arm (tokens, raw text, final text, and segments_sha256 = segment and word text with start/end ms); identical_native / identical_ref = every token field with p and plog bitwise (informational: p and plog are floats, no identity is claimed); p_max_abs and err (plog max_abs/rel_l2 against ref) quantify them. equal_ref = tokens_equal_ref and text_equal_ref and final_equal_ref. output_sha256 = sha256 of the final text. work.transcript and work.final_text are real text from public benchmark audio under benchmarks/data/ only. mel_equal_dump / states_equal_dump compare an arm's own mel and encoder states with the dump's digests (diagnostic). A failed arm call has elapsed_us null and work.error; the command exits nonzero on any failed call, any candidate output that differs from the dump ref or the same-row native, any native A/A inconsistency (tokens, text, segments) or an incomplete grid, and keeps the file, whose last line is run_end.
run_meta.order: passes 0...passes, pass 0 warmup; rows in dump index order; pass p, row index r runs Williams sequence (p + r) mod 6 of order_sequences (every arm leads, and immediately follows every other arm, equally often); seq is the global execution order
